Family holidays in Carinthia, Austria

Explore the mountains together. Without the summer crowds.

Our Panorama Lodge is made for families: three bedrooms (yes, with bunk beds), a big table for cosy evenings and a park with a pool and playground. The lake and the mountains are right around the corner.

Adventure for the whole family!

Why spring or autumn?

More time together, less queuing

No queues

Outside July and August it's quiet at the lifts, on the trails and by the lake. More space to explore together.

Half-term friendly

Spring and autumn fit perfectly with May and October half-term. A short, active break in the mountains.

Room for everyone

A detached chalet with three bedrooms. The kids get their own room, you sleep peacefully in the main bedroom.

Everything on the park

A heated outdoor pool (mid-May to early October), wooden playground, air trampoline and a restaurant. The lakeside beach borders the park.

Free +CARD Holiday

Stay between mid-May and November and you get the +CARD: free regional buses and free summer mountain lifts on the Nassfeld, plus discounts across the region.

For kids

Something fun for every age

From splashing to climbing: our favourites for kids aged 4 to 16.

Ages 4–8

Splash and discover

  • Aqua Trail on the NassfeldA 1.5 km play trail on the mountain: build dams, play with fountains and climb aboard a real sailing boat. June to September.
  • On and around the parkPlayground, air trampoline, an Escape Box and the Yuki treasure hunt. In season, the heated outdoor pool and Schluga lake beach with a water inflatable, free with the orange wristband.
  • Adventure park by the lakeA slide into the lake, mini cars and a kids' zone. Late June to mid-September.

Ages 9–12

Speed and adventure

  • Pendolino summer tobogganRide the gondola up and race 2 km down Carinthia's longest summer toboggan run. June to September.
  • Garnitzenklamm gorgeWaterfalls, little bridges and a geo trail through the gorge. Wear sturdy shoes!
  • Paddleboarding and cyclingOut on the lake on a SUP board, or cycling through the flat Gailtal valley.

Ages 13–16

Challenge and views

  • Nassfeld Outdoor ParkRock labyrinth, flying fox and 3D archery. Daily in June and September in good weather, late May and October on request.
  • Climb a real summitReach a summit cross together, with views across the border into Italy.
  • Day out in VillachShopping, ice cream and cafés in the region's biggest town.

Opening times vary by season and year. Check nassfeld.at before you go.

Seasons

What to do each season

May half-term

Around Lake Presseggersee

5.9 km on the flat through the reeds, about an hour and a half. Easy for little legs.

From mid-May

+CARD Holiday

From mid-May you get the +CARD on arrival: free buses around the region and free rides on the summer mountain lifts.

Mid-May

Carinthian Hiking Opening

The region opens the hiking season with a festive weekend in the nearby Lesachtal valley.

April–June

Cycling the Gailtal valley

Flat valley routes, ideal for kids on their own bikes. E-bikes can be hired locally.

From June

Aqua Trail and Pendolino

Once the mountain lifts open in June: play on the Aqua Trail first, then toboggan back down.

All spring

Fossil hunting

In the Carnic Alps Geopark you walk across ancient seabed. Who'll find the first fossil?

Dates and opening times vary from year to year. See nassfeld.at for the current programme.

Winter sports

Skiing on the Nassfeld

We ski on the Nassfeld every year ourselves: Carinthia's largest and sunniest ski area, a short drive from the lodge. According to the region it gets around 100 more hours of sunshine than the northern Alps.

110 kmof pistes: 30 km blue, 69 km red, 11 km black
± 30lifts and gondolas, up to around 2,000 m
7.6 kmthe Carnia valley run, the longest run in the area
Dec – Aprski season, 4 December to 4 April in 2026/27

Up with the Millennium Express

From Tröpolach the gondola takes you up in three sections to almost 1,900 m. The ski bus stops a few hundred metres from the park, so you can leave the car behind.

Skiing with kids

Four secured children's areas with magic carpets, ski schools for kids from age 4 and childcare from 2.5 years. Children under 10 get free ski equipment, and some weeks have extra children's discounts.

Our regular routine

We always start at the Millennium Express and rent a ski locker at the bottom, so there's nothing to carry. Then après-ski at Zum Alois, right by the valley station.

More than skiing

Tobogganing on the natural runs at Guggenberg (2 km) and Weissbriach (3 km), 90 km of cross-country trails, 160 km of winter walking paths and snowshoeing.

Skating on Lake Weissensee

In winter Lake Weissensee becomes Europe's largest prepared natural ice surface (6.5 km²). It's also where the Dutch skate their Alternative Elfstedentocht. Check the ice report first.

Handy on the park

A ski drying room (for a fee), fresh bread rolls at reception and a park shop for groceries.

Season dates, lift times and discounts vary from year to year. See nassfeld.at for current information.

Day trips

Möderndorf, near Hermagor

Garnitzenklamm gorge

A gorge about 4.5 km long with waterfalls, sheer rock walls and emerald pools. Open in the warmer months; some sections need sure footing.

More info ↗

Lake Presseggersee

Paddleboarding on the lake

Glide over the calm, clear water on a SUP board. Lovely on a mild spring or autumn day.

City day out

Villach and Klagenfurt

Two charming Carinthian towns for a day of shopping, cafés and culture.

Warmbad-Villach

Kärnten Therme

Thermal water park with slides, a crazy river and its own area for little ones. Open all year, ideal on a rainy day.

More info ↗

Landskron Castle, near Villach

Monkey Mountain and Eagle Arena

Around 180 Japanese macaques in a large outdoor enclosure, with a bird of prey show at the castle just above. April to October.

Practical

Austria

Required in your car

A warning triangle, a high-vis vest for every passenger, an in-date first-aid kit and a motorway vignette (digital from ASFINAG or at a petrol station before the border). Police do sometimes check.

About us

Our little spot in the mountains

Our holiday home grew out of our love for nature and the peace of the mountains. Time together with family and friends: for us, those are the moments that really count.

When we had the chance to buy a house at EuroParcs Pressegger See, everything fell into place. The location, the atmosphere and the mix of lake, mountains and activities were exactly what we were looking for.

EuroParcs takes care of everything on site. So you can count on local service and a warm welcome, and we're always happy to share tips.

Warm wishes, Sander & Maud
